terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Not solved; review camera is fixed by the consumer harness.

objectClass.primaryType: small heap of six dried cranberries
objectClass.notes: Matte faceted clay shading, flat color facets only. Identity carried by silhouette (flattened oblate) + carved crease geometry, not color -- mesh=1, simplest material budget in the batch alongside choco.

reasoning: Six near-identical macro bodies differing only in XZ offset/yaw and crease-sector rng draw, so componentCount scores 1.
Silhouette scores 2 (not 1): the carved crease groove is a real, load-bearing silhouette/normal feature, more than olive/choco's smooth taper alone.
Repetition density scores 1: 6 instances, hand-placed, matching the batch's established scale.
materialLayerCount scores 0: only 1 material bucket needed -- both secondary hex dropped (crease now geometric, blush free-via-lighting).
Local detail density scores 1: crease + flatten deformation are the only two authored details.
Occlusion risk scores 1: interior/back berries' far sides are hidden but inferable by near-symmetry.
Action readiness scores 0: static turntable showcase prop.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Simple tier, macro-only (no mask split needed since crease is a deformation, not a second material), one repetition system for the 6-instance mound.

detailInventory.note: Enumerated by hand from the three supplied reference views -- CRIB.md skip rule for single-repeated-system objects.

details.observation: Every berry shows 1-2 fold-crease grooves running along its flattened top surface, parallel to the long axis, not radiating from a pole.
details.inference: Dried-fruit wrinkle -- the defining identity signal distinguishing cranberry from a smooth berry.

details.observation: Berries read as flattened discs/lentils, not spheres -- height distinctly less than width.
details.inference: Drying flattens the berry; distinguishes from the perfectly round blueberry in the same batch.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: six-berry mound silhouette with all six individually readable
visible longitudinal fold crease per berry
faceted flat shading baked into geometry

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Six-berry mound silhouette, all individually readable
Visible longitudinal fold crease on top surface
All six berries rest on the shared ground, no floating parts

droppedPasses.lighting-pass: lighting is fixed by the consumer harness and is not authorable in the model
droppedPasses.interaction-pass: static showcase prop with no sockets, hinges or colliders beyond a bounding proxy

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: Consumer runtime keeps only map and color; repo bans PBR maps outright.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold

lightingPass.authority: Lighting is fixed by the consumer: scripts/breadlab.ts mirrors scripts/thumbsHarness.ts with a warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2) intensity 1.4, an ambient 0xfff0dc at 0.75 and a cool fill 0xdce8ff at (2.5, 3, -2) intensity 0.2.
mustAvoid: relying on a contact shadow the harness does not render

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The runtime normalizes the cluster's longest axis to 1.6, so absolute dimensions are arbitrary.
Exact crease count/position per berry is not identity-critical at pixel precision; the flattened silhouette + at-least-one-visible-crease read is what the review scores.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z, the direction the harness three-quarter camera at (-1.6, 2.2, 2.6) looks from
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: CRANBERRY_RADIUS = 0.5 relative unit. Absolute scale is meaningless: the consumer runtime refits the cluster's longest axis to 1.6 (types.ts section 6).

silhouette.boundingShape: compact hex-packed mound of six flattened oblate berries, roughly 2.7 wide by 0.75 tall by 1.9 deep in relative units
silhouette.symmetry: each berry is approximately radially symmetric before the crease pull and flatten deformations break it slightly; the cluster as a whole is asymmetric
dominantCurves: smooth oblate curve, flattened on the vertical axis
negativeSpaces: longitudinal fold-crease grooves on each berry's top surface
shallow contact creases where berries touch
landmarks: 1-2 fold creases per berry, always facing world-up regardless of yaw

observations: six oblate near-round berries in a compact touching mound, individually readable
each berry shows 1-2 longitudinal fold creases on its visible top surface, not radiating from a pole
silhouette is flattened/plump, not spherical -- distinguishes from blueberry in the same batch
berries read as flattened discs/lentils, height distinctly less than width
fold creases run roughly horizontally across the visible face, parallel to the long axis
six roughly oval footprints packed into a compact cluster
creases visible on the top faces run along the long axis of each berry, confirming the front-elevation read

localFeatures.name: Six-berry hex-packed mound
localFeatures.description: Six berries placed with independent XZ offsets and yaw in a compact hex-packed arrangement (types.ts R1); all six share the ground plane at world Y=0 after each instance's own bounding-box floor correction.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: faceted planar shading from split vertices, including the carved crease grooves
surfaceDetail.displacementPattern: crease grooves carried as vertex-position pull-toward-axis on fixed (ring,sector) grid indices, zero extra triangles
surfaceDetail.occlusionPattern: none -- runtime Lambert has no AO channel; crease darkness comes from facet-normal N.L falloff alone
surfaceDetail.notes: Assembly node; no surface of its own.

componentTree.name: Cranberry (a)
componentTree.topologyRationale: One continuous rotationally-built mass, laid on its side (rotateZ bake, olive precedent) so the flattened radialScale axis becomes world-up and the profile's pole-to-pole axis becomes the long horizontal axis. Fold creases are a (ring,sector) grid vertex pull-toward-axis on the same shell, not a separate part.

deformationStack.notes: radialScale sx=0.75 (old local X, becomes world-up after lay-down) vs sz=1.0 -- flattens the berry vertically without touching the long axis.
Sectors [4, 5, 6] (sectorCenter+-1, faces world-up after lay-down per olive's cap convention) pulled toward the local axis by 28% of local radius on every non-pole ring, before jitter.
One rng-chosen sector per berry (excluding the primary cluster), pulled toward the axis by a shallower amount -- organic per-instance variation, deterministic under the builder rng.
amplitude 0.016 (0.032 of radius), applied indexed after the crease pulls.

geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: flat normals baked by splitting vertices after jitter, never a flatShading flag

collider.notes: Oblate bounding proxy; sufficient for a static showcase prop.

materials.name: Cranberry body (deep saturated crimson)
materials.shaderModel: MeshStandardMaterial carrier; the consumer runtime swaps it for MeshLambertMaterial keeping only map and color

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: No texture is emitted. UVs exist only for merge attribute consistency.

roughness.localResponse: inert -- the runtime Lambert swap discards roughness entirely

ambientOcclusion.notes: No AO channel: the runtime Lambert material has none.

localOverrides.name: Crease facet-normal shading
localOverrides.description: No second dark bucket is authored for the crease shadow hex (#8E2438); the carved groove's own facet normals already darken under the runtime key light, the same mechanism cracker's docking holes use.

localOverrides.name: Per-face key-light highlight
localOverrides.description: No bright bucket is authored for the upper-face blush hex (#D9707F); the runtime key light's N.L falloff already brightens upper-facing facets for free (olive/choco precedent).

shaderNotes: Emit via scripts/breads/lib.ts stdMaterial(): MeshStandardMaterial with roughness 1, metalness 0.
Never set vertexColors: the runtime rebuilds every material as MeshLambertMaterial({map, color}).
Never set flatShading: that flag is not inherited by the runtime swap either. Faceting must be baked as split vertices.
materials.notes: Single solid color for the whole cluster; identity carried entirely by silhouette + carved crease geometry (types.ts inherited section 9). mesh=1.

repetitionSystems.name: Six-berry hex-packed mound
repetitionSystems.elementKind: repeated macro body, single-mesh lay-down shell with carved creases each

distribution.mode: hand-placed XZ offsets with independent yaw; crease always faces world-up post-layout regardless of yaw (yaw only rotates about the vertical axis)
distribution.note: Offsets read off cranberry-3.png (top-down footprint); berry-f carries an extra tiltZ for visual variety (olive-a precedent).

repetitionSystems.seedRule: Offsets/yaw are fixed authored values; surface-jitter and the secondary-crease sector selection consume the builder rng, so the exported GLB is byte-deterministic.

acceptance: Silhouette reads correctly without materials.
Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

featureReviews.notes: 6 individually readable oblate berries in a tight hex-packed mound; count and general pile arrangement match cranberry.png/cranberry-3.png.
FLATTEN_X=0.68 gives a distinctly flattened lumpy silhouette (not spherical) on shot-90/180/270, matching cranberry-2.png's flattened-disc read.

v3 (cmp-3.png, after 2 depth/taper iterations): tapered single-sector V-notch (center depth 0.6, neighbors 0.08) reads as a clear dark fold line on most berries, a large improvement over the v1/v2 broad shallow dip that read as generic low-poly bumpiness.
All six berries sit flush on y=0, no floating parts on any orbit angle.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Hard consumer budget for the 'cluster' ingredient group: <=700 tri and <=68KB target (types.ts R2), hard ceiling <=2500 tri and <=100KB. Target reached by construction (10 segments x 6 profile-ring transitions x 6 berries = 540 tri; crease pulls add zero triangles), not by decimation.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2), intensity 1.4, upper-left.
lightingFromPhoto.exposure: no exposure control, no tone mapping.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Ambient 0xfff0dc at 0.75 -- crease darkening relies on facet-normal orientation away from the key light, not a painted shadow.

proceduralStrategy: Build each berry vertically (olive convention) via buildRevolvedShell with radialScale sx=0.75 (flatten) sz=1.0.
Pull (ring,sector) grid vertices toward the local axis for the primary (sectorCenter+-1) and one rng-chosen secondary crease sector, on the indexed pre-layout shell.

Bake lay-down via rotateZ(-90deg) so the pole-to-pole axis becomes world-X (long axis) and the flattened radial axis becomes world-Y (up) -- the crease then faces world-up regardless of per-instance yaw.
Jitter vertices while still indexed, after the crease pulls.
Bake faceting by splitting vertices and recomputing normals; never request flatShading.
Project top-planar UVs, then merge all six berries into exactly one mesh (single material, no mask split needed).
Translate each instance's own bounding box floor to world Y=0 after its per-instance yaw/tiltZ rotation.
animationAnchors: root pivot supports whole-cluster rotation for the showcase turntable
each berry is a named instance
destructionAnchors: each berry is its own fractureGroup; the only plausible break is one berry rolling away from the heap

risks.description: assets/prompts/ingredients/cranberry.json names a crease-shadow hue (#8E2438) this spec does not paint as a color region.
risks.mitigation: Crease is now real carved geometry; its own facet normals darken under the runtime key light for free (cracker docking-hole precedent), so a painted tone would double-darken.

risks.description: The upper-face blush hex (#D9707F) is not painted into geometry.
risks.mitigation: Runtime key light N.L falloff already brightens upper-facing facets (olive/choco precedent).

risks.description: A crease pattern radiating from a pole would misread as pumpkin, a separate ingredient in this same 12-item batch.
risks.mitigation: Crease is carved BEFORE the lay-down rotation on a fixed (ring,sector) column, producing a groove parallel to the long/flattened axis after layout, not a pole-radiating pattern -- verified against cranberry-2/-3.png front/top views before implementation.

risks.description: Any vertex-color-based region paint is silently discarded by the runtime's MeshLambertMaterial swap.
risks.mitigation: Single flat material bucket authored; no vertexPaint block anywhere in this spec.

risks.description: A flatShading flag is not inherited by the runtime material swap.
risks.mitigation: Faceting is baked into geometry by splitting vertices before export.
